html:
The Southern Pomo lived along the Russian River and its side valleys in today's Sonoma County, northern California, around Healdsburg, Santa Rosa and Sebastopol. Their language, Southern Pomo, is one of seven distinct Pomoan languages, and keeps more of the old Proto-Pomo word forms than its sisters.

They gathered acorns, fished the river and made fine baskets. Their neighbours were the Kashaya on the coast, the Coast Miwok to the south and the Wappo to the east. From 1817 the missions at San Rafael and later Sonoma drew people in, and Mexican ranchos took the valleys. Today Southern Pomo people belong to the Dry Creek and Cloverdale rancherias and, together with Coast Miwok, to the Federated Indians of Graton Rancheria.
